text: We collected two and a half million sales calls and studied them with a machine learning platform at scale. What we found is that anywhere between 40 and 60% of the average salesperson's qualified pipelines will be ultimately marked as closed loss, no decision.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Lenny asks Matt to explain the research methodology behind his books on sales. Matt describes their massive data collection effort during the pandemic when sales moved to virtual platforms, allowing them to analyze millions of sales conversations. He reveals a surprising finding about how many qualified sales opportunities - not just random leads, but real prospects that salespeople have invested time in - end up being lost not to competitors, but to customer indecision where prospects simply disappear without making any decision.
text_ko: 우리는 250만 건 이상의 영업 콜을 모아 대규모 머신러닝 플랫폼(machine learning platform)으로 분석해봤어요. 그 결과 평균 영업사원의 퀄리파이드 파이프라인(qualified pipelines) 중 약 40~60%가 최종적으로 클로즈드 로스(closed loss)·노 디시전(no decision)으로 표시되더라고요.
text_zh: 我们收集了250万通销售通话，并用机器学习平台(machine learning platform)做了大规模分析。结果显示，平均每个销售人员的合格商机(qualified pipelines)中，大约有40%到60%最终会被标为输单/无决定(closed loss, no decision)。
text_es: Recopilamos dos millones y medio de llamadas de ventas y las estudiamos a gran escala con una plataforma de aprendizaje automático (machine learning). Lo que descubrimos es que entre el 40% y el 60% del pipeline calificado (qualified pipeline) del representante de ventas promedio termina marcado como "cerrado — pérdida, sin decisión" (closed loss, no decision).
key_sentence: 46% of qualified pipelines will be marked as closed loss, no decision.
original_text: We collected two and a half million sales calls and studied them with a machine learning platform at scale. What we found is that anywhere between 40 and 60% of the average salesperson's qualified pipelines will be ultimately marked as closed loss, no decision. If you think about as a salesperson, that for 46% of your deals, you're going to spend a lot of time, energy, resources pursuing these opportunities where you eventually just get ghosted.

vocabulary.definition: A subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn from data and improve their performance over time without being explicitly programmed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, machine learning is often utilized to analyze large datasets, automate decision-making processes, and enhance customer experiences through predictive analytics.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of advanced technology and innovation, often associated with cutting-edge applications in various industries.

vocabulary.definition: A sales term referring to potential sales opportunities that have been vetted and deemed likely to convert into actual sales.
vocabulary.businessContext: Qualified pipelines are crucial for sales teams as they help prioritize leads and allocate resources effectively to maximize revenue generation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a level of assurance regarding the likelihood of closing a sale, making it more favorable than simply referring to all leads.

vocabulary.definition: A status assigned to a sales opportunity that has been pursued but ultimately did not result in a sale, often due to the customer deciding not to proceed.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding closed loss metrics helps businesses analyze their sales processes and identify areas for improvement in their sales strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a negative connotation, indicating a missed opportunity, and is often used in discussions about sales performance and forecasting.

text: Dialing up the FOMO backfires 87% of the time. They're not afraid of missing out, they're afraid of messing up. What salespeople have been armed to do is go out and dial up the FOMO and make the customer sweat a little bit.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Matt explains a key insight from analyzing millions of sales calls about why traditional sales tactics fail. When customers hesitate before making a purchase decision, most salespeople try to create urgency by emphasizing what the customer will miss out on (FOMO - fear of missing out). However, Matt's research shows this approach actually makes things worse 87% of the time because customers aren't worried about missing opportunities - they're terrified of being personally blamed if the purchase decision goes wrong.
text_ko: 놓칠까 봐 불안함(FOMO)을 더 자극하면 87%의 경우 역효과가 나요. 사람들은 놓치는 걸 두려워하는 게 아니라, 결정을 잘못해 망칠까 봐 더 걱정해요. 그런데 영업사원들은 바로 그걸 하도록 훈련받아서 FOMO를 부추기고 고객을 조금 긴장시키게 해요.
text_zh: 放大错失恐惧(FOMO)的做法在87%的情况下会适得其反。客户并不是怕错过，他们是怕把事情搞砸。现在的销售被教成要去放大这种FOMO，让客户出点汗。
text_es: Avivar el miedo a perderse algo (FOMO) resulta contraproducente el 87% de las veces. No les da miedo perderse algo; les da miedo equivocarse. A los vendedores se les ha dicho que salgan a avivar ese miedo y a meterle un poco de presión al cliente.
key_sentence: They're not afraid of missing out, they're afraid of messing up.
original_text: Dialing up the FOMO backfires 87% of the time. They're not afraid of missing out, they're afraid of messing up. What salespeople have been armed to do is go out and dial up the FOMO and make the customer sweat a little bit. The FOMU actually matters more than the FOMO. The FOMU is the fear of messing up.

vocabulary.definition: To have an unexpected and undesirable outcome, especially after a planned action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strategy or tactic that backfires can lead to negative consequences, such as loss of customer trust or decreased sales.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies that the initial intention was positive, but the results were counterproductive.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals whose primary role is to sell products or services to customers, often through direct interaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: Salespeople are crucial in driving revenue for a business, as they engage with potential clients and persuade them to make purchases.
vocabulary.nuance: While the term is neutral, it can carry a connotation of being persuasive or aggressive, depending on the sales approach.

text: The first thing is we've got to judge their level of indecision. The second thing is we've got to offer a recommendation.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Lenny asks Matt about his JOLT method for improving sales processes based on his research insights. Matt explains that JOLT is an acronym for a four-step approach to help customers overcome their fear of making bad decisions. The method addresses the core problem that customers want to buy but can't because they're paralyzed by fear of failure, so salespeople need to systematically reduce that fear and guide them toward a decision they feel confident about.
text_ko: 먼저 그들이 어느 정도 망설이고 있는지 파악해야 해요. 그다음엔 우리가 추천안(recommendation)을 제시해야 해요.
text_zh: 第一，我们要判断他们犹豫不决到什么程度，第二，我们要给出建议。
text_es: Lo primero es evaluar su grado de indecisión. Lo segundo, ofrecerles una recomendación.
key_sentence: we've got to judge their level of indecision.
original_text: The first thing is we've got to judge their level of indecision. The second thing is we've got to offer a recommendation. The third thing is we've got to get them to start trusting us and we call it limit the exploration, and the T is we've got to de-risk the deal. We've got to take some risk off the table.

vocabulary.definition: A suggestion or proposal aimed at advising someone on a course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, recommendations are often made to guide decision-making processes, particularly in areas such as marketing strategies, product development, or management practices.
vocabulary.nuance: While a recommendation implies a level of authority or expertise, it is often more persuasive than mandatory, leaving room for the recipient's discretion.

vocabulary.definition: The inability to make a decision quickly or confidently, often resulting in procrastination or inaction.
vocabulary.businessContext: Indecision can hinder progress in business environments, particularly during negotiations or strategic planning, where timely decisions are crucial for success.
vocabulary.nuance: Indecision may carry a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of confidence or clarity, and is typically viewed unfavorably in fast-paced business contexts.

text: Most salespeople are trying to figure out what's keeping the customer up at night. The challenger approach is about showing the customer what should be keeping them up at night. What's a risk that they don't know about but you do.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Matt contrasts traditional sales approaches with his Challenger Sale methodology. Traditional salespeople focus on identifying existing customer problems and pain points. The Challenger approach flips this - instead of just responding to what customers already know they need, top salespeople proactively educate customers about risks and opportunities they haven't considered yet. This works because salespeople talk to many more customers and have broader market insight than any individual buyer.
text_ko: 대부분의 영업사원들은 고객이 밤잠을 설치게 하는 게 뭔지 알아내려고 해요. 챌린저 접근법(challenger approach)은 고객이 잠 못 이루게 해야 할 문제를 보여주는 거예요. 고객은 모르는데 당신은 알고 있는 위험은 뭐예요?
text_zh: 大多数销售都在想办法弄清楚，到底是什么让客户夜里睡不着。挑战者方法(Challenger approach)则是在向客户指出，真正该让他们担心的是什么。有什么风险是他们还没意识到、但你已经看见的？
text_es: La mayoría de los vendedores intentan averiguar qué les quita el sueño a los clientes. El enfoque challenger (Challenger) consiste en mostrarles aquello que en realidad debería quitarles el sueño. ¿Qué riesgo no ven ellos pero sí tú?
key_sentence: The challenger approach is about showing the customer what should be keeping them up at night.
original_text: Most salespeople are trying to figure out what's keeping the customer up at night. The challenger approach is about showing the customer what should be keeping them up at night. What's a risk that they don't know about but you do. You are a window into the outside world for them, and that's what challengers really understand.

vocabulary.definition: A sales strategy that involves educating customers about potential risks and opportunities they may not be aware of, thereby challenging their current thinking.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and sales, the challenger approach is used to differentiate a salesperson by positioning them as a trusted advisor who provides insights that provoke thought and drive change in customer behavior.
vocabulary.nuance: This approach is often used when traditional sales tactics fail to resonate, emphasizing the importance of understanding the customer's underlying issues rather than just their stated needs.

vocabulary.definition: The possibility of loss, damage, or any negative outcome that may arise from a decision or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding and managing risk is crucial for decision-making, as it affects everything from investment strategies to project management and operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While risk often carries a negative connotation, it can also represent opportunities for growth and innovation when managed effectively.

text: Indecision stems from their fear of failure. The omission bias is the fact that people don't want to be blamed for making decisions that lead to a loss.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Matt explains the psychological research behind customer indecision, drawing from cognitive psychology studies. He describes 'omission bias' - a powerful human tendency where people prefer losses that happen from inaction over losses that result from their active decisions. This bias is even stronger than status quo bias (preferring to keep things the same). Understanding this helps explain why customers who want to buy a product still hesitate - they're not worried about missing benefits, they're terrified of being personally blamed if their purchase decision leads to problems.
text_ko: 우유부단함은 실패에 대한 두려움에서 비롯돼요. 부작위 편향(omission bias)은 사람들이 손실로 이어지는 결정을 내려 비난받는 걸 피하려고 차라리 아무 행동도 하지 않으려는 성향을 말해요.
text_zh: 犹豫不决往往源于害怕失败。不作为偏见（omission bias）是指人们宁可不做决定，也不愿意因为自己的决定导致损失而被怪罪。
text_es: La indecisión nace del miedo a fracasar. El sesgo de omisión (omission bias) consiste en que la gente prefiere no tomar decisiones porque no quiere que le echen la culpa si acaban en pérdidas.
key_sentence: The omission bias is the fact that people don't want to be blamed for making decisions that lead to a loss.
original_text: Indecision stems from their fear of failure. The omission bias is the fact that people don't want to be blamed for making decisions that lead to a loss. There are losses that happen when we do nothing, and then there are losses that happened because we did something. In the human mind, people are okay with missing out. They are not okay with messing up and being blamed.

vocabulary.definition: Indecision refers to the inability to make a choice or decision, often due to uncertainty or fear of the consequences. It can lead to procrastination and missed opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, indecision can hinder strategic planning and slow down project execution, as team members may hesitate to commit to a course of action.
vocabulary.nuance: Indecision often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of confidence or clarity, and is typically avoided in high-stakes environments.

vocabulary.definition: Omission bias is a cognitive bias where individuals prefer to avoid actions that could lead to negative outcomes, even if inaction may result in worse consequences. It reflects a tendency to favor inaction over action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, omission bias can affect decision-making processes, leading teams to avoid necessary risks or innovations due to fear of accountability for negative results.
vocabulary.nuance: This bias can subtly influence group dynamics, as individuals may collectively lean towards inaction to evade blame, which can stifle progress.

text: We found a technique called pings and echoes that high performers use.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Matt describes a specific technique discovered in their research for the first step of the JOLT method - judging a customer's level of indecision. The 'pings and echoes' technique works like sonar - salespeople send out a 'ping' by suggesting what many customers worry about at this stage, then listen for the customer's response (the 'echo') to understand their specific concerns. This approach works because customers often won't directly admit they're indecisive or afraid, so salespeople need a subtle way to surface these concerns without embarrassing the customer.
text_ko: 성과가 높은 사람들이 쓰는 '핑과 에코(pings and echoes)'라는 기법을 발견했어요.
text_zh: 我们发现表现优秀的人常用一个技巧：先提醒一下、再确认反馈（pings and echoes）。
text_es: Descubrimos una técnica llamada "pings y echoes" (pings and echoes) que usan los que mejor rinden.
key_sentence: pings and echoes that high performers use.
original_text: We found a technique called pings and echoes that high performers use. The way this works is that a salesperson will try to articulate but in a non, not to out the customer, but to get confirmation or refutation that what they've articulated is actually a concern for their buyer. At this point, most customers like you, are thinking about this or they're worried about that.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or teams that consistently achieve exceptional results or exceed established standards in their work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, high performers are often recognized for their contributions to productivity, innovation, and overall success, making them valuable assets to organizations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting not only competence but also a strong work ethic and commitment to excellence.

vocabulary.definition: A specific method or way of doing something, often involving skill or expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, techniques can refer to strategies or processes employed to enhance efficiency, productivity, or innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'technique' implies a level of skill, it can also suggest a systematic approach that may be replicated or taught.

text: What great salespeople do though is they know that while they'll stand by those claims, those case studies, those proof points, they try to kind of under-promise and over-deliver.
speaker: Matt Dixon
context: Matt explains a key technique for the final step of JOLT - taking risk off the table for nervous customers. When customers get excited about impressive case studies showing dramatic results, average salespeople let them build high expectations. However, top performers deliberately reset expectations to more conservative but guaranteed outcomes. This reduces the customer's fear that they won't achieve the promised results and get blamed for the purchase. By setting lower expectations, salespeople make it more likely the customer will feel confident about the decision and be pleasantly surprised by the actual results.
text_ko: 훌륭한 영업사원들은 그런 주장들이나 사례 연구(case studies), 증빙 포인트(proof points)를 지지하고 책임진다는 건 알지만, 약속은 일부러 낮게 잡아 기대 이상으로 보여주려고 해요 (under-promise and over-deliver).
text_zh: 优秀的销售人员知道，虽然他们会为那些说法、那些案例 (case studies) 和证明点 (proof points) 负责，但会尽量少承诺、多兑现。
text_es: Lo que hacen los mejores vendedores es que saben que, aunque respalden esas afirmaciones, esos casos de éxito (case studies) y esas evidencias (proof points), tienden a prometer menos y luego entregar más.
key_sentence: Great salespeople under-promise and over-deliver while standing by those claims.
original_text: What great salespeople do though is they know that while they'll stand by those claims, those case studies, those proof points, they try to kind of under-promise and over-deliver. What I'd rather we do is build your business case around a 5X improvement because we see that at least that, in 100% of our implementations. Then, let's set up to over-deliver against that.

vocabulary.definition: To set expectations lower than what one believes can be achieved, often to avoid disappointing stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, under-promising is a strategy used to manage client expectations, ensuring that the actual outcomes exceed what was initially communicated.
vocabulary.nuance: This approach is often favored in competitive environments where over-promising can lead to reputational damage.

vocabulary.definition: To provide results or outcomes that exceed the initial expectations set for a project or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, over-delivering is a tactic used to enhance customer satisfaction and build long-term relationships by surprising clients with better-than-expected results.
vocabulary.nuance: While over-delivering can strengthen client trust, it should be done judiciously to avoid setting unsustainable future expectations.

vocabulary.definition: Specific pieces of evidence or data that support a claim or assertion, demonstrating its validity or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales and marketing, proof points are crucial for convincing potential clients of the value of a product or service, often presented in the form of statistics or testimonials.
vocabulary.nuance: The effectiveness of proof points relies on their relevance and credibility, making it essential to choose them carefully.

vocabulary.definition: In-depth analyses of specific instances or examples that illustrate how a product or service has been successfully implemented or utilized.
vocabulary.businessContext: Case studies are frequently used in business to showcase successful applications of a product, helping to build trust and demonstrate real-world results to potential customers.
vocabulary.nuance: While case studies are powerful marketing tools, they should be representative and not cherry-picked to maintain credibility.
